content.text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"MA","level":"state","category":"rent_increase_limits","status":"in_force","title":"General prohibition on rent control with limited municipal option under Chapter 40P Section 4","requirement":"No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation only if: (1) after six months from initial adoption, compliance by property owners is entirely voluntary and uncoerced; (2) regulation may not include occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or removal of properties from regulation; (3) regulation may not apply to rental units owned by entities owning fewer than ten rental units or units with fair market rent exceeding $400; and (4) municipality must compensate owners for the difference between fair market rent and rent-controlled rent from general funds.","citation":"Mass. Gen. Laws c. 40P, § 4","quoted_span":"No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides: (a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced, and the property of a person or entity declining to have his or its property subjected to such regulation shall be wholly unaffected by any aspect of the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation; (b) such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400; and (c) a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds, so that the cost of any rent control shall be borne by all taxpayers of a municipality and not by the owners of regulated units
